Below is a **generic recipe** you can adapt to almost any REST‑style “download manager” API. I’ll show you what the request usually looks like, how to authenticate with your `dload_key`, and how to pull out just the *file ID* (plus whatever extra metadata the provider returns). --- ### 1️⃣ What the API probably expects | Element | Typical value | |---------|---------------| | Base URL | `https://api.downloads.com/v1` *(or similar)* | | Endpoint | `/files` or `/downloads` – the resource that lists all download records | | Query parameters | `domain=downloads.com` (to filter by source), `page=`/`limit=` for paging | | Auth method | Most services use either:
• API Key in a custom header (`X-Api-Key`)
• Bearer token in the Authorization header `Authorization: Bearer dload_key` | If the docs say otherwise, swap it out—just keep the same idea. --- ### 2️⃣ Sample Python snippet (using `requests`) ```python import requests BASE_URL = "https://api.downloads.com/v1" ENDPOINT = "/files" # <-- adjust if the real path differs DOMAIN = "downloads.com" HEADERS = { "Accept": "application/json", "Content-Type": "application/json", # Either one works depending on the API spec: "X-Api-Key": "dload_key", # Custom header style # OR #"Authorization": f"Bearer {dload_key}" # Token style } PARAMS = { "domain": DOMAIN, "per_page": 100, # optional: number per page # "page": 1 # optional: start at first page } def fetch_file_ids(): ids_and_meta = [] url = BASE_URL + ENDPOINT while True: resp = requests.get(url, headers=HEADERS, params=PARAMS) resp.raise_for_status() # will raise error if status != 200 data = resp.json() # Assuming the payload structure is something like: # {"data":[{"id":"abc123","name":"foo.zip"}, ...], "meta":{"next_url": "..."}} for item in data["data"]: record = { "id": item["id"] } # Add any additional context attributes you care about # e.g., timestamp, size, mime type, etc. for attr in ("created_at", "size_bytes"): if attr in item: record[attr] = item[attr] ids_and_meta.append(record) # Pagination handling – stop when there's no next link/page meta = data.get("meta") if not meta or not meta.get("next_url"): # depends on API design break # If the API uses cursor/pagination tokens instead of URLs: # PARAMS.update({"cursor": meta['next_cursor']}) return ids_and_meta if __name__ == "__main__": results = fetch_file_ids() print(f"{len(results)} files found.") for r in results[:5]: # preview first five print(r) ``` #### Why this pattern? | Step | Reason | |------|--------| | **Headers** | Keeps auth separate from body/query so you’re less likely to hit rate limits or accidental leaks. | | **Params** | Filters by domain right away, reducing bandwidth & processing time. | | **Pagination loop** | Handles huge result sets without blowing memory. Adjust according to whether the API gives you a `next_url`, a cursor/token, or simple numeric pages. | | **Selective extraction** | Pull only `"id"` plus any useful keys (`created_at`, `size_bytes`, etc.) – nothing else. | --- ### 3️⃣ Things to double‑check against the official documentation | Item | Checkpoint | |------|------------| | **Endpoint name/path** | Some providers expose `/downloads/list` or `/records`. | | **Auth scheme** | Confirm whether they want a bearer token or a plain key header. | | **Query parameter names** | Might be `source_domain`, `filter[domain]=…`, or even a POST body. | | **Response shape** | Look for top‑level keys like `items`, `results`, or nested under `payload`. | | **Rate limiting** | Respect `Retry-After` headers or backoff guidelines. | | **Error codes** | Handle 401/403 for bad keys, 429 for throttling, 500+ for server hiccups. | --- ### 4️⃣ Quick sanity test Run the script locally after replacing placeholders. You should see output resembling: ``` 1200 files found. {'id': 'f9a7b8e3', 'created_at': '2024-04-12T08:23Z'} {'id': 'c34de56f', 'created_at': '2024-04-11T14:07Z'} ... ``` That’s it! Once you confirm the exact field names and endpoints, plug them into the skeleton above and you’ll have a clean list of file IDs (with any chosen context attributes) ready for downstream processing.
